alex: Quick follow-up to the cursor/pagination RFC — I've sketched a smaller, opt-in surface that might avoid the iterator vs resume debate. Thoughts?

maria: TL;DR?

alex: idea: unify all SDKs around a single simple pagination primitive: `fetch_page(cursor?: string, page_size?: int)` that returns `{ items: [...], next_cursor?: string, retry_after?: ms }`. No streaming iterator in the core. Higher-level helpers can compose iterators for Python/TS. Go gets the raw primitive.

sam: That sounds straightforward. Main tradeoff is who owns retry semantics for a paged call — SDK or transport?

alex: I'm proposing transport-level retries only for idempotent page fetches when the server returns retryable errors. But we attach an explicit idempotency token per page call so server can dedupe. So SDK will always pass `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` for page requests it retries internally.

jen-ml: How do we handle resume tokens that encode server state (e.g., shard snapshot)? Previously we had complex resume logic because tokens could be tied to ephemeral state.

alex: The new rule: server-controlled cursors are opaque and may become invalid; clients must treat `next_cursor` as best-effort. If server returns `410 CursorExpired`, SDK surfaces that as a typed error `CursorExpiredError` and higher-level iterator can either restart from a checkpoint or fail. We document non-guarantees so no hidden magic.

maria: Can you paste a small example of the header/response shape?

alex: Sure:

```
Request: GET /v1/items?page_size=100&cursor=eyJv...
Headers: Idempotency-Key: 3f2d7c9a-...

Response 200:
{
  "items": [...],
  "next_cursor": "eyJv...",
  "estimated_remaining_ms": 42
}
```

sam: What about streaming endpoints (server push) used by some ML workloads for long lists?

alex: Keep streaming separate. Streaming stays `stream()` on runtime transports. Pagination primitive is for bounded page fetches only. This separation avoids mixing retry semantics: stream = no auto-retry, page = retry with idempotency token.

jen-ml: Are we sure we want the SDK to generate idempotency keys automatically? For server-side metrics and quotas it's useful, but might hide when callers want manual control.

alex: We generate them by default for retries, but we expose a `idempotencyKey` override parameter so advanced callers can supply their own. Default helps most users.

maria: Backwards compatibility: we have customers using iterator.resume() heavily. Migration path?

alex: Provide compatibility shim in next minor: `iterator()` will be implemented on top of `fetch_page`. For Python/TS we ship `auto_iterator` helper that keeps minimal state and maps `CursorExpiredError` into a callback hook so apps can decide. We'll mark old `resume()` experimental-deprecate in 6 months.

sam: Perf concern: will wrapping iterator over repeated `fetch_page` increase RT tail due to extra round trips?

alex: Not significantly for typical page sizes. If customers need lower latency, recommend using streaming or larger page_size. Also transport can multiplex multiple page requests in flight if caller sets `concurrency` on iterator helper.

jen-ml: Testing plan?

alex: Add unit tests for header emission, idempotency override, typed errors. Integration tests: server sim that returns intermittent 5xx and duplicate-apply detection when idempotency key reused. E2E: sample app migrating iterator -> fetch_page.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for eng-platform on 2026-02-12 22:00 UTC (per rollout policy). :rocket:

maria: ok, this seems pragmatic. My only ask: document the failure modes clearly in the SDK docs (CursorExpired, PartialPage, RetryAfter). Also add a small migration guide.

alex: Will draft the follow-up RFC + changelog note today, and open implementation PRs for py/ts/go. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
